abstract: Chapter 10 of the Mahabharata unveils Drona's Tactics — a moment that tests the moral, spiritual, and philosophical limits of its characters. Through vivid narrative and timeless wisdom, this chapter reveals the stakes of dharmic living.
objectives: Understand the key events and their moral significance in Drona's Tactics.
Analyse the choices made by Drona and their consequences.
Connect the chapter's philosophical teachings to the Bhagavad Gita's framework.
Identify the central dharmic dilemma and its resolution.
highlights: Drona's Chakravyuha trap kills the young Abhimanyu
The breaking of war convention marks the beginning of adharma on the field
Yudhishthira is forced to lie — destroying the aura of his dharmic life
Drona is slain in grief for his son — a grief manufactured as a weapon

characters.name: Drona
characters.role: Brilliant teacher caught between duty and grief

characters.name: Yudhishthira
characters.role: Forced to utter a half-lie — his first moral fall

characters.name: Abhimanyu
characters.role: Young hero trapped in Chakravyuha and slain

content_blocks.content: The narrative of Chapter 10 — Drona's Tactics — begins with a pivotal moment that ripples through the entire epic. The characters involved are not merely actors in a tale; they are archetypes of the universal human condition, each embodying a fragment of cosmic truth.

content_blocks.english_translation: Even a teacher who is confused about right and wrong must be corrected.
content_blocks.content: This verse from Chapter 10 captures the essential teaching embedded in Drona's Tactics. Meditate on it as you study the events that follow.

The central dharmic dilemma of Chapter 10: Drona must choose between personal desire and universal duty. This choice — repeated throughout the Mahabharata — is the heartbeat of the epic's moral philosophy.

By the end of Drona's Tactics, the reader understands that the Mahabharata is not a story about war. It is a story about the war within — the battle between ego and truth, between attachment and liberation, between what we desire and what is right.
Remember: the Mahabharata teaches that every action (karma) creates its ripple in time. What Drona does in Chapter 10 echoes across every subsequent chapter of the epic.

glossary.definition: Liberation from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth — the ultimate aim of all dharmic action.
